name: Kemezung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Both descriptions READ via the Internet Archive (Cox 2005 Notes on the Phonology of Kemezung; Smoes 2010 Sketch Grammar): 3-level tone system described, no word-stress statement anywhere in either.

sources.citation: Cox, Bruce. 2005. Notes on the Phonology of Kemezung. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. iii+17 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.4 Tone (printed p.7-8): 'Kemezung has three contrastive tone levels: high, mid and low'; contours analysed as level-tone sequences; TBU = mora. Sections on syllable types, root structure (roots 1-2 syllables, C2 restrictions) and noun/verb tone patterns; no mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Smoes, Christopher L. 2010. A Sketch Grammar of the Kemezung Language. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. iv+47 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: No phonology chapter (nouns, verbs, clauses only). Only 'stress' token is emphatic: 'the greater the amount of stress placed on the particle nə, the further in the past the speaker refers to' (printed p.27, sec. 3.2.1) -- not a word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Smoes, Christopher L. 2014. A Summary Analysis of the Discourse Structure of the Kemedzung Language. SIL Cameroon. 54 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing; discourse analysis; 'prominence' refers to participant prominence.

sources.citation: Cox, Bruce. 2005. Kemezung Orthography Guide. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 16 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; alphabet, vowels/length, sec. 3 Tone (orthographic tone marking) only.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory GM 1412 Kemezung (Green & Moran, source Cox 2005).
sources.note: Segment/tone inventory only, derived from Cox 2005; no stress information.
Consonants, 9 vowels, 7-8 tones; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Brye, Edward & Elizabeth Brye. 2004. Intelligibility testing survey of Bebe and Kemezung and synthesis of sociolinguistic research of the Eastern Beboid cluster. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2004-011.
Brye, Edward & Elizabeth Brye. 2002. Rapid appraisal and intelligibility testing surveys of the Eastern Beboid group of languages (Northwest Province). SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-019.
sources.note: Only remaining Glottolog-listed item not opened; a sociolinguistic survey, very unlikely to contain a stress statement (the 2004 companion report has no phonology).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. The Bantoid languages: a monograph (draft). Text copy already held by the project under bish1246.
sources.note: Mentions Cox (2005) as the phonology of Kemezung and gives a comparative wordlist column; no stress/accent statement for Kemezung or Eastern Beboid (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0 relevant hits).
